mainTopic: Items left to one who owes הקדש, the end of שום היתומים, and consecrating an inherited field near the יובל
overview: This amud finishes the chapter שום היתומים and begins a new chapter. First the גמרא explains several lines of the משנה about סידור בערכין. A poor person who owes an ערך is left his basic needs, based on the פסוק 'ואם מך הוא מערכך'. The same word הוּא shows that his wife and children are not included. It then explains why the רבנן do not let a farmer keep his oxen, and why the משנה needed to teach the single-tool case and רב יימר's ruling about תפילין in a sale. A new משנה teaches that the treasurer may not take the clothing of a man's wife and children, and that הקדש values items only by their present place and time. A ברייתא gives the פסוק for this. After the הדרן, a new משנה gives timing rules for consecrating and redeeming an inherited field near the יובל. רב and שמואל explain that the two-year rule is money-saving advice, not a ban. Then they argue about consecrating in the יובל year itself, and the גמרא defends שמואל by tying his view to רבי שמעון.

steps.title: The verse teaches: keep him alive from the ערך
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads the פסוק 'ואם מך הוא מערכך' as an instruction to leave the poor person enough to live on, taken from the money he owes.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'But if he is too poor for your valuation.' Read it as: keep him alive from your valuation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the source from the תורה for the משנה's rule that we leave a poor person food, clothing and other basics before collecting his ערך.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word הוּא ('he') is read as if it were connected to the word for 'life' (חיים). So the פסוק is telling the treasurer: sustain him out of what he owes. That is why the treasurer may not take everything he owns.

keyTerms.meaning: A fixed amount set by the תורה that a person pledges to give to הקדש
Poor, too low in money to pay
Keep him alive, sustain him
Arranging a poor person's payment so that he keeps his basic needs

steps.whyThisMatters: This derasha is the foundation for the whole idea that a debtor to הקדש keeps his basic needs.

phrases.english: "But if he is too poor for your valuation"
Sustain him from your valuation.
phrases.notes: The word הוּא is being read like the word for 'life,' so the פסוק means: keep him alive out of what he owes.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם מָךְ הוּא מֵעֶרְכֶּךָ הַחֲיֵיהוּ מֵעֶרְכֶּךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens this part by giving the source for the משנה's rule of סידור בערכין.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The treasurer must leave the poor person enough to live on, taken from his ערך obligation.

steps.title: Why not his wife and children?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line that the basics are left only for him and not for his wife and children, and asks for the reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: but not for his wife and his children. What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה and asks for its source. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה limits the leftover basics to the man himself. The גמרא wants to know what in the פסוק excludes his family, since they also need to eat.

keyTerms.meaning: His wife and his children
What is the reason?

phrases.english: But not for his wife and his children, etc.
What is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל לֹא לְאִשְׁתּוֹ וּבָנָיו מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next detail of the משנה, still using the same פסוק.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for leaving out the wife and children from סידור בערכין.

steps.title: The word 'he' excludes the family
steps.stepSummary: The word הוּא in the פסוק means only he is sustained from the ערך, not his wife and children.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'he... from your valuation.' That means he is sustained, but not his wife and children.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the word הוּא ('he') limits the rule to the man himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same word that taught us to sustain him (step 1) also narrows the rule. It says 'he,' not 'he and his household,' so only his own basic needs are protected.

keyTerms.meaning: 'He': read here as limiting the rule to the man alone

steps.whatToRemember: One word, הוּא, does two jobs: it teaches that we sustain the poor person, and that only he is sustained, not his family.

phrases.english: "He... from your valuation,"
and not his wife and his children from your valuation.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוּא מֵעֶרְכֶּךָ וְלֹא אִשְׁתּוֹ וּבָנָיו מֵעֶרְכֶּךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word הוּא limits the sustenance to the man himself, so his wife and children are not included.

steps.title: Why do the רבנן disagree about the farmer's oxen?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי אליעזר, who says a farmer keeps his pair of oxen, and asks why the רבנן do not agree.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: if he was a farmer, the treasurer gives him his pair of oxen. And the רבנן, why don't they agree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רבי אליעזר's view in the משנה and asks for the reasoning of the רבנן who argue. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה already lets a craftsman keep his work tools. רבי אליעזר treats a farmer's oxen the same way. So why would the רבנן take them away?

keyTerms.meaning: A farmer who plows fields
His pair (of oxen) used for plowing
And the רבנן? (What is their reason?)

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:
If he was a farmer,
he gives him his pair [of oxen].
And the Rabbis?
phrases.notes: He means: why don't the רבנן agree that he keeps his oxen?

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר אִם הָיָה אִיכָּר נוֹתֵן לוֹ צִמְדּוֹ וְרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new line in the משנה: the argument about the farmer.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason the רבנן do not let the farmer keep his oxen.

steps.title: Animals are property, not tools
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן hold that oxen and donkeys are not tools of a trade but regular property, so the treasurer may take them.
steps.simpleTranslation: These animals are not tools of a craft. They are property.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the רבנן: animals are not counted as work tools, so they can be collected for the ערך.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees that tools of a trade are left for him. The argument is only about how to classify work animals: רבי אליעזר sees them as tools, while the רבנן see them as ordinary possessions.

keyTerms.meaning: Tools of a craft or trade
Property, possessions

steps.whatToRemember: The argument is not whether tools are protected. It is whether work animals count as tools.

phrases.english: These are not tools of craft,
rather, they are property.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנְהוּ לָאו כְּלֵי אוּמָּנוּת נִינְהוּ אֶלָּא נְכָסִים נִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The רבנן classify work animals as property, not as tools of a craft, so they are not left for him.

steps.title: Why teach the case of only one tool? It is obvious
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's case of someone who has only one tool of a certain type, and asks why it needed to be taught: if one was enough until now, it is enough now.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: if he had one of a type. Isn't that obvious? Just as one was enough for him until now, now too it is enough for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the need for this line of the משנה, saying the ruling is obvious. The next step answers this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה rules that we do not sell his extra tools of one type to buy more of a type he has only one of. The גמרא argues that this needs no teaching: he managed with one until now, so he can keep managing with one.

keyTerms.meaning: One type (of tool)
It is obvious! (Why did it need to be said?)
It is enough for him

steps.confusionAlert: פשיטא is not saying the משנה is wrong. It is asking why the משנה bothered to teach something that seems obvious.

phrases.english: If he had one of a type.
It is obvious!

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הֵיכִי דְּסַגִּי לֵיהּ עַד הַשְׁתָּא,
phrases.english: Just as it was enough for him until now,
now too it is enough for him.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָיָה לוֹ מִין אֶחָד פְּשִׁיטָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next line of the משנה and challenges whether it was needed.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling about a person who has only one tool of a certain type.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If one tool of that type was enough for him until now, it is obviously enough now, so the משנה did not need to teach it.

steps.title: Why the single-tool rule needed to be taught
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers its question from step 6. We might have thought one tool is no longer enough, because now that he is poor no one will lend him a second one. So the משנה teaches that one tool is still enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: until now, when he had things of his own to lend to others, people would lend to him in return. But now that there is no one who will lend to him, one tool is not enough. So the משנה teaches us that it is still enough.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question: why did the משנה need to say that a person with only one tool keeps just that one?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question was: if one tool was enough until now, it is enough now. The answer shows a real reason to think otherwise. Before, he could borrow a second tool in exchange for lending his own, but now he has nothing left to lend. The משנה rejects this worry and leaves him with only one.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said: this sets up a mistaken idea that the teaching comes to remove
to lend
It teaches us: this is the new point the teaching adds

steps.whatToRemember: The single-tool rule is not extra. It teaches that we do not give him more tools just because he can no longer borrow.

phrases.english: You might have said:
until now, when he had things to lend to others,
people would lend to him;
now that there is no one who will lend to him,
one tool is not enough. So it teaches us that it is enough.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 6 by showing why the single-tool ruling teaches something new.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows a reason we might have thought otherwise (מהו דתימא), so the teaching is needed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Now that he cannot borrow, the treasurer should leave him an extra tool.
steps.terutzMaskana: He keeps only the one tool. We do not worry that he can no longer borrow.

steps.title: רב יימר takes the תפילין of a man who sold his property
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that the treasurer takes the תפילין of one who consecrates his property. Then it tells a story: a man sold all his property, and רב יימר ruled that his תפילין go to the buyer too.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: one who consecrates his property, they take his תפילין. A certain man sold all his property. He came before רב יימר, who said to them: take off his תפילין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new line from the משנה about תפילין and tells a story about a sale. This sets up the next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה speaks about consecrating property to הקדש. The story is about selling property to a regular buyer. רב יימר ruled the same way for the sale: the תפילין are part of 'all his property.'

keyTerms.meaning: one who consecrates his property to the Temple (הקדש)
tefillin
who sold them
take off / remove

phrases.english: One who consecrates his property,
they take his tefillin.
A certain man who sold his property
came before Rav Yeimar.
He said to them: Take off his tefillin.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַמַּקְדִּישׁ אֶת נְכָסָיו מַעֲלִין לוֹ תְּפִילִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new line of the משנה about תפילין.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone who sells all his property must also hand over his תפילין, just like one who consecrates his property.

steps.title: Why do we need the story if the משנה already says it?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the story of רב יימר: what new thing does it teach? The משנה already says plainly that the תפילין are taken.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is this story teaching us? It is already a משנה: one who consecrates his property, they take his תפילין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רב יימר's ruling is worth telling, since the משנה already says the same thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a story only repeats a משנה, it seems to add nothing. The challenge assumes that selling and consecrating work the same way. The answer will show that they might not.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it teaching us? Used when something seems to add nothing new
It is (already) a משנה

phrases.english: What is this teaching us?
It is already a mishna!
"One who consecrates his property, they take his tefillin."

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן? מַתְנִיתִין הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the story in step 8 as adding nothing to the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need to report רב יימר's ruling
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה already rules that תפילין are taken, so the story seems to teach nothing new.

steps.title: Selling is different from consecrating
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that we might have thought the תפילין are included only when consecrating, because then he feels he is doing a מצוה. When selling, a person would not usually give away the things he uses for his own מצוות. So the story teaches that a sale includes the תפילין too.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: only there, when he consecrates, are the תפילין included, because he thinks, 'I am doing a מצוה.' But when it comes to selling, a person does not sell a מצוה he does with his own body. So the story teaches us that even in a sale the תפילין are included.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what רב יימר's story adds beyond the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With הקדש, the man is giving to the Temple, so he is glad to include even his תפילין. With a sale, we might guess he meant to keep his personal מצוה items. רב יימר's ruling teaches that 'all his property' includes the תפילין even in a sale.

keyTerms.meaning: there, in the other case (here: consecrating)
selling
a מצוה done with one's own body, like תפילין

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two cases. The משנה is about consecrating to הקדש. The story of רב יימר is about selling to a regular person, and that is why it was needed.
steps.whatToRemember: תפילין are included in 'all his property' both when consecrating and when selling.

phrases.english: You might have said:
it is only there that the tefillin are included, since he thinks:
"I am doing a מצוה";
but when it comes to selling,
a person does not sell a מצוה of his own body.
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the word in square brackets is the corrected wording. Both mean 'sell.'

phrases.english: So it teaches us that they are included.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא, הָתָם הוּא דְּסָבַר מִצְוָה קָא עָבֵידְנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 9 by pointing out a difference between consecrating and selling.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points out a difference between the case in the משנה and the case in the story
steps.terutzHavaAmina: In a sale, a person keeps his תפילין, since he would not sell a personal מצוה item.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even in a sale of all his property, the תפילין go to the buyer.

steps.title: The treasurer may not take the clothing of the wife and children
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה teaches that whether a person consecrated his property or valued himself, the treasurer may not take his wife's or children's clothing. This includes clothes he dyed for them and new sandals he bought for them.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Both one who consecrates his property and one who values himself have no claim to the clothing of his wife, or the clothing of his children, or clothing he dyed for them, or new sandals he bought for them.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists items that belong to the wife and children, so the treasurer may not take them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule covers both cases: הקדש and ערכין. It goes beyond clothes they already wear. Even dyed garments and new sandals bought for them belong to them, so they are not part of the man's property.

keyTerms.meaning: one who pledges his own ערך (fixed Torah value) to הקדש
clothing / garment
dyed clothing
for their sake, meant for them

steps.whyThisMatters: It adds to the rule from steps 2–3 that only the man himself is cared for. Even so, what already belongs to his wife and children stays with them.

phrases.english: MISHNA: Both one who consecrates his property
and one who values himself,
have no claim to the clothing of his wife,
nor to the clothing of his children,
nor to clothes he dyed for them,
nor to new sandals that he bought for them.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ אֶחָד הַמַּקְדִּישׁ נְכָסָיו, וְאֶחָד הַמַּעֲרִיךְ עַצְמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה about items belonging to the wife and children.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The treasurer may not take the clothing of the wife or children, clothes dyed for them, or new sandals bought for them.

steps.title: The treasury gets only the current place and time value
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues: even though a slave, a cow or a pearl could bring a higher price with better clothing, on market day, or in the big city, the הקדש values things only by where and when they are now.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even though people say that a slave sells for more in good clothes, a cow sells for more on market day, and a pearl sells for more in the big city, the Temple treasury only gets the item's value at its present place and time.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה from step 11 continues with a new rule about how the treasurer values the property he collects. He values it as it is, here and now.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gives three examples where waiting or improving the item would raise its price. Even so, the הקדש does not get that extra value. It is only owed the item's worth at its current location and current time.

keyTerms.meaning: A coin worth one hundred דינר
The market day, when buyers are many and prices are high
A big walled city, where goods sell for more
A pearl
Its place and its time, meaning its value here and now

phrases.english: Even though they said:
slaves sell for more when sold in their clothing,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאִם תִּלָּקַח לוֹ כְּסוּת בִּשְׁלֹשִׁים דִּינָר
phrases.english: for if a garment is bought for him for thirty dinar
he goes up in value by a hundred dinar,

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן פָּרָה אִם מַמְתִּינִין אוֹתָהּ לָאִיטְלֵיס
phrases.english: and likewise a cow, if they wait with it until market day
it is worth more,

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן מַרְגָּלִית אִם מַעֲלִין אוֹתָהּ לַכְּרַךְ
phrases.english: and likewise a pearl, if they bring it up to the big city
it is worth more —
the Temple treasury has only its place and its time.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאָמְרוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same משנה about what the treasurer collects, now adding how the items are valued.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Items collected by הקדש are valued only by their present location and present time, not by a higher price they could fetch later or elsewhere.

steps.title: The verse source for valuing an item as it is today
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from the words 'on that day' that the value is fixed now. A pearl is not held back waiting for people who would take it to a better market.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: 'And he shall give the valuation on that day.' This means he does not hold a pearl waiting for people who would sell it somewhere for more.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that gives the פסוק behind the משנה's rule of 'its place and its time'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'on that day' (ביום ההוא) tie the payment to the present moment. So the item is valued right away, as it is now, and nobody waits for a better buyer or a better market.

keyTerms.meaning: Your valuation, the set amount owed to the הקדש
On that day, meaning the value is set now
Delay, hold back
Literally 'light ones', people who would carry the pearl to sell it elsewhere

phrases.english: Gemara: The Rabbis taught:
"And he shall give the valuation on that day"
that he should not hold back a pearl for the 'light ones',
phrases.notes: Literally 'the light ones': people who would carry the pearl off and sell it where it fetches more.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: וְנָתַן אֶת הָעֶרְכְּךָ בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the פסוק source for the משנה's rule in step 12.
steps.raayaObject: The משנה's rule that הקדש only gets the item's value at its present place and time.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The words 'on that day' in ויקרא 27:23.

steps.title: Unspecified consecrations go to Temple upkeep
steps.stepSummary: The same ברייתא learns from 'holy to the Lord' that when someone consecrates without saying what for, it goes to בדק הבית.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Holy to the Lord': this teaches that consecrations with no purpose stated go to the upkeep of the Temple building.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with the next words of the same פסוק and learns a new rule from them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a separate teaching from the one in step 13. If a person just says 'my property is consecrated' and gives no purpose, the property goes to the fund for repairing the בית המקדש, not to the כהנים.

keyTerms.meaning: Consecrations where no purpose was stated
The fund for upkeep and repair of the בית המקדש

steps.whatToRemember: The הקדש gets an item's value here and now ('on that day'), and a consecration with no stated purpose goes to בדק הבית ('holy to the Lord').

phrases.english: "Holy to the Lord"
phrases.notes: The next words of the same פסוק, ויקרא 27:23.

phrases.english: unspecified consecrations go to Temple upkeep.

steps.triggerLanguage: קֹדֶשׁ לַה׳ סְתָם הַהֶקְדֵּישׁוֹת לְבֶדֶק הַבַּיִת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא, learning a second rule from the next words of the פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A consecration with no stated purpose goes to בדק הבית.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing פרק שום היתומים
steps.stepSummary: The chapter שום היתומים ends with the traditional closing line.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, chapter 'שום היתומים'.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the closing formula for the chapter. It marks that the chapter is finished.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן is not part of the argument. It is a farewell line said at the end of a פרק, showing love for the learning and a hope to come back to it.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you, said when finishing a chapter
'The appraisal of the orphans', the name of the chapter now ending

phrases.english: We will return to you,
'The Appraisal of the Orphans'.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲדַרַן עֲלָךְ שׁוּם הַיְּתוֹמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter that the previous steps were part of.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The chapter שום היתומים is complete.

steps.title: Consecrating and redeeming an inherited field near the יובל
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה rules that a person may not consecrate a field less than two years before the יובל, may not redeem it less than one year after the יובל, and the partial year is counted in favor of the הקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: One may not consecrate a field less than two years before the יובל, and one may not redeem it less than one year after the יובל. When figuring the price, we do not count months to help the owner, but the treasury does count months to help itself.
steps.whatsHappening: A new chapter begins with a new משנה about a field a person inherited and consecrated, and how its timing relates to the יובל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The price to redeem such a field depends on how many years are left until the יובל. The משנה gives timing limits for consecrating and redeeming. It also says that a leftover partial year is not split into months to lower the price for the owner, though the הקדש may count months when that helps the treasury.

keyTerms.meaning: The Jubilee, the fiftieth year, when inherited fields go back to their families
A field a person inherited from his family
Redeem, buy back from the הקדש
Count months, splitting a year into parts when figuring the price

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה does not say the word 'field', but it is talking about a field a person inherited. The time limits here are about that kind of field, not about every kind of consecration.

phrases.english: Mishnah: One may not consecrate
phrases.notes: He means a field the person inherited from his family.

phrases.english: less than two years before the Jubilee,
and one may not redeem after the Jubilee
less than one year.
One does not count months against the Temple treasury,
phrases.notes: So the owner cannot lower his price by paying only for part of a year.

phrases.english: but the Temple treasury does count months.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ אֵין מַקְדִּישִׁין לִפְנֵי הַיּוֹבֵל פָּחוֹת מִשְׁתֵּי שָׁנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the new chapter after the הדרן.
steps.whyThisMatters: These timing rules for consecrating and redeeming an inherited field are the base text that the גמרא is about to question and explain.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An inherited field is not consecrated less than two years before the יובל nor redeemed less than one year after it, and partial years are counted in the הקדש's favor only.

steps.title: A ברייתא contradicts the משנה about consecrating before the יובל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that allows consecrating a field any time before or after the יובל. This seems to clash with the משנה, which forbids consecrating less than two years before the יובל.
steps.simpleTranslation: The גמרא raises a contradiction: a ברייתא teaches that one may consecrate either before the יובל or after it. In the יובל year itself one should not consecrate, and if he did, the field is not consecrated!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets the ברייתא against the משנה. The ברייתא says any time before the יובל is fine, while the משנה says not less than two years before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה (step 16) seemed to forbid consecrating within two years of the יובל. The ברייתא only excludes the יובל year itself, so consecrating even a few months before seems allowed. Both cannot be read as strict rules, so the גמרא needs an explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: And they contradicted it: the גמרא sets one source against another
One may consecrate (to הקדש)
The יובל year, the fiftieth year, when fields return to their owners
It does not become holy; the consecration does not take effect

phrases.english: Gemara: And they raised a contradiction:
One may consecrate both before the Jubilee
and after the Jubilee,
but in the Jubilee year itself one should not consecrate,
and if he did consecrate, it is not consecrated!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּרְמִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the משנה of step 16 with a ברייתא that seems to say the opposite.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that one may not consecrate a field less than two years before the יובל.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא allows consecrating any time before the יובל and only excludes the יובל year itself. That seems to contradict a two-year limit.

steps.title: The two-year rule is advice, not a ban
steps.stepSummary: רב and שמואל explain that the משנה only means there is no reduced redemption price within two years of the יובל. So a person should not consecrate then, to protect his own money.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב and שמואל both say: one does not consecrate in order to redeem with a deduction when less than two years remain. Since that is so, a person should take care of his property and not consecrate less than two years before.
steps.whatsHappening: רב and שמואל resolve the contradiction. The משנה is not saying the consecration fails. It is warning the owner that he will lose money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually the redemption price is lowered for the years already passed, a reduction called גירוע. With less than two years left there is no reduction, so he would pay the full price for very little time. Consecrating then is legally valid, as the ברייתא says, but the משנה advises against it.

keyTerms.meaning: To be redeemed (bought back from הקדש)
Deduction, the lowered redemption price for the years that have passed
Is careful about his property; does not waste his money
Both of them

steps.whatToRemember: Consecrating a field less than two years before the יובל is valid. The משנה only advises against it because there is no גירוע, so the owner would lose money.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'one may not consecrate' in the משנה as a real ban. רב and שמואל explain it as practical money advice. The consecration still works.

phrases.english: Rav and Shmuel, who both say:
One does not consecrate to be redeemed with a deduction
less than two years before,
and since one does not consecrate
to be redeemed with a deduction less than two years before,
a person should be careful with his property
and not consecrate less than two years before.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב וּשְׁמוּאֵל דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction of step 17 by reinterpreting the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the משנה: advice instead of a ban
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to say consecration less than two years before the יובל is forbidden or does not work.
steps.terutzMaskana: It works. There is just no גירוע, so a sensible person avoids it to save money.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the difference between whether something takes effect and whether it is wise. That distinction sets up the next question, about the יובל year itself.

steps.title: רב and שמואל disagree about consecrating in the יובל year itself
steps.stepSummary: רב holds that a field consecrated during the יובל year is holy and redeemed for the full fifty. שמואל holds that it is not holy at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: if someone consecrates his field in the יובל year itself, רב says it is consecrated and he pays fifty, and שמואל says it is not consecrated at all.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new dispute about consecrating during the יובל year itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our ברייתא said such a consecration is not holy, which matches שמואל. רב says it takes effect, with no deduction at all, so redemption costs the full fifty shekels. This is the price for a field that needs a כור of seed.

keyTerms.meaning: His field; here an inherited field, a שדה אחוזה
He pays fifty: the full redemption price of fifty shekels
At all; not even a little

phrases.english: It was stated:
One who consecrates his field
in the Jubilee year itself,
Rav says: it is consecrated, and he gives fifty,
phrases.notes: Fifty is the full price the תורה sets, fifty shekels for a field needing a כור of seed, with nothing taken off.

phrases.english: and Shmuel says:
it is not consecrated at all.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר: הַמַּקְדִּישׁ שָׂדֵהוּ בִּשְׁנַת הַיּוֹבֵל עַצְמָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up the ברייתא's last clause about the יובל year itself and shows that it is disputed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: consecration in the יובל year is valid and redeemed for the full fifty. שמואל: it is not valid at all.

steps.title: רב יוסף begins challenging שמואל: the קל וחומר works for selling
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף grants that for selling a field in the יובל year, שמואל's view makes sense through a קל וחומר. This sets up his challenge about consecration.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף objects: I understand that regarding selling, where שמואל disagrees with רב, one can make a קל וחומר. If a field that was already sold goes back to its owner now, then surely a field that was not yet sold cannot be sold now.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the setup of רב יוסף's challenge. He first shows where שמואל's view does have logic, namely selling. Next he will ask why consecration should be any different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the יובל year, sold fields return to their owners. So a new sale in that year obviously cannot work. That קל וחומר supports שמואל for sale, and רב יוסף is about to question whether the same reasoning works for הקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: Objects to it; raises a strong challenge
Granted; it makes sense. It sets up an 'but here...' question
Sale
An argument from a weaker case to a stronger case
Is it not logical? The closing words of a קל וחומר

phrases.english: Rav Yosef objects to this:
Granted, regarding a sale,
that Shmuel disagrees with Rav,
phrases.notes: רב and שמואל also argue about selling a field during the יובל year. שמואל says the sale does not work.

phrases.english: one can say an a fortiori argument:
if a field that was already sold
goes out now,
phrases.notes: It leaves the buyer and returns to the original owner in the יובל year.

phrases.english: then one that is not sold,
is it not logical that it cannot be sold?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב יוֹסֵף: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְעִנְיַן מְכִירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts challenging שמואל's view from step 19 by first granting the logic for selling.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that consecration in the יובל year is not valid at all.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The קל וחומר explains why a sale fails in the יובל year. רב יוסף is setting up the point that this reasoning may not carry over to consecration, so שמואל would lack a source there.

steps.title: For a consecrated field, the קל וחומר seems to fall apart
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף asks whether a קל וחומר can work for הקדש. A משנה says that when the יובל comes and the field was not redeemed, the כהנים take it but pay its value, according to רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But here, with consecration, can you really make a קל וחומר? We learned in a משנה: if the יובל arrived and the field was not redeemed, the כהנים enter it and pay its value. These are the words of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף completes his challenge to שמואל. He argues that the קל וחומר that worked for selling a field does not work for consecrating one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a sale, a field sold before the יובל goes back to its owner for free at the יובל, so a sale made during the יובל surely does not take hold. With הקדש, according to רבי יהודה, the הקדש never loses for free, because the כהנים pay its value. So there is no 'weakness' at the יובל to build a קל וחומר on, and שמואל's ruling that the consecration does not take hold seems to have no basis.

keyTerms.meaning: An argument from a lighter case to a stricter one: if it is true here, it is surely true there
It was redeemed (bought back from הקדש)
The כהנים enter it, meaning they take possession of the field
Its value or price

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not whether the כהנים get the field. רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון both agree they do. The question is whether they pay the הקדש for it, because that decides whether the הקדש 'loses' at the יובל.

phrases.english: But here,
phrases.notes: 'Here' means the case of consecrating a field, in contrast to selling one.

phrases.english: is there a kal vachomer to be said?
But didn't we learn in a mishnah:
If the Jubilee arrived and it was not redeemed,
the priests enter into it
and pay its value,
these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא הָכָא, מִי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר קַל וָחוֹמֶר? וְהָא תְּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב יוסף's challenge that began in step 20, contrasting הקדש with sale.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that a field consecrated in the יובל year is not holy
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קל וחומר needs the field to leave הקדש for free at the יובל. According to רבי יהודה the כהנים pay its value, so the הקדש loses nothing and there is no basis for the קל וחומר.

steps.title: שמואל follows רבי שמעון: the כהנים take the field without paying
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that שמואל holds like רבי שמעון, who says the כהנים take the field at the יובל but do not pay for it. So the field does leave הקדש for free, and the קל וחומר works.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל holds like רבי שמעון, who says: 'They enter, but they do not pay.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends שמואל by saying he follows רבי שמעון instead of רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי שמעון, a field consecrated before the יובל leaves the הקדש at the יובל without any payment. Then the קל וחומר works again: if the יובל undoes a consecration made earlier, surely a consecration made during the יובל year itself does not take hold. This rescues שמואל's view from רב יוסף's challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds, meaning this is his opinion
They enter but do not pay, meaning the כהנים take the field for free
Consecrated property, or the Temple treasury

steps.whatToRemember: The whole dispute depends on whether the כהנים pay at the יובל. Under רבי יהודה they pay, so there is no קל וחומר. Under רבי שמעון they do not pay, so there is a קל וחומר, and שמואל follows רבי שמעון.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that שמואל's ruling is tied to an earlier תנאים dispute, so his view is not baseless.

phrases.english: Shmuel holds in accordance with Rabbi Shimon,
who says: 'They enter, but they do not pay.'

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁמוּאֵל כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן סְבִירָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב יוסף's challenge from step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Tying the view to a different תנא (שמואל follows רבי שמעון, not רבי יהודה)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב יוסף's challenge assumed רבי יהודה's view, that the כהנים pay, so the קל וחומר fails.
steps.terutzMaskana: שמואל follows רבי שמעון, so the field leaves הקדש for free at the יובל, and the קל וחומר holds.
